identity.title: Structural Determinants Underlying the Interplay Between Fatty Acid Binding and S-Nitrosylation of Human Serum Albumin.

content.abstract: Human serum albumin (HSA) is a multifunctional protein whose biological properties are determined not only by its amino acid sequence but also by a complex interplay of functional sites, post-translational modifications, and endogenous ligands. However, the structural mechanisms by which these regulatory factors influence the functional state of HSA remain insufficiently understood. The aim of this study was to investigate the structural basis of the interplay between HSA functional regions, using Cys34 S-nitrosylation and fatty acid (FA) binding as model regulatory processes. For this purpose, the structural features and conformational dynamics of FA-free and FA-loaded native and nitrosylated HSA, as well as their interactions with glutathione (GSH) and S-nitrosoglutathione (GSNO), were studied using molecular docking and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Changes in the overall structure of HSA after incubation with GSNO were assessed by (1)H NMR spectroscopy. MD analysis revealed that FA binding alters the conformational dynamics of HSA and affects the structural environment of Cys34 and other functionally significant regions. These FA-induced effects were further modulated by S-nitrosylation, which influenced the conformational landscape of albumin in a manner dependent on its fatty acid-bound state. The similarity of the one-dimensional (1)H NMR spectra of HSA before and after incubation with GSNO suggests the absence of pronounced changes in the overall protein structure upon interaction with the nitrosylating agent. The obtained data provide insights into how FA binding and S-nitrosylation shape the conformational properties of HSA through modulation of the structural environment of Cys34 and other functionally significant regions. The results highlight the importance of considering post-translational modifications and endogenous ligands as key determinants of HSA structure-function relationships.
